deck.title: Putting AI To Work: Friday Labs Live Training

content.title_html: How business owners are putting AI to work across their <accent>entire company</accent>, without learning to code or hiring a single engineer.

content.text: By the end of today, you'll know three things...

lines: How AI really evolved, and what just changed
Why most business owners are about to use it wrong
What it actually takes to put AI to work

content.question: Stay to the very end. There's something I'm only putting on the table for the people who are here live tonight.
content.hint: You'll know it when you see it. It's worth the wait.

content.reason: The people who take notes are the people who act.

content.label: business owners follow this work. This is what I teach them

content.text: Quick intro. Then we go deep.
I'm Tyler Germain.

The scene and its light are concentrated in the upper-right of the frame; the lower-left falls into deep near-black shadow. content.overlay_text: For three years, my job has been one thing: putting AI to work inside real businesses.

content.label: building AI automation systems for real businesses

content.headline: $10M+ brands. Agencies. Ecom. SaaS. Every kind of business.

content.label: businesses I've helped put AI to work

content.claim_html: I'm not here to sell you on AI. <accent>I'm here to show you how it actually works.</accent>

content.callout_html: Most business owners are about to make the same expensive mistake with AI. <accent>I'd rather you didn't.</accent>

content.label: This is for you if
items: You run a business doing $250K to $20M a year
You know you should be using AI but haven't had the time
You're tired of generic tools that don't fit how you actually work

content.label: This is NOT for
items: Pre-revenue founders with no business to run yet
Anyone who just wants a chatbot on their website
People shopping for the cheapest possible thing
The four eras of AI, and the one that just changed everything
The three things that make AI actually work in a business
What it takes to put it all together

content.text: But first...
You have to understand one thing about what AI even is now.
Here's the thing.

content.claim_html: AI isn't a tool you add to your business. <accent>It's an operating system you install.</accent>

content.text: A tool does one task. An operating system runs everything.

content.text_html: And how you install that operating system <accent>just completely changed.</accent>

content.label: Most owners think
content.belief: AI is that chatbot I tried once. It wasn't all that impressive.

content.text: They formed their opinion of AI two years ago. Two years is forever right now.

content.label: Every quarter you wait
consequences: A competitor installs their system first
Your team stays buried in work AI should be doing
The gap stops being something you can catch

content.text_html: If I could show you how it actually works today, <accent>would you put it to work?</accent>

content.text: To see where AI is going, you have to see where it's been.

visual.prompt: A very dark, near-black sheet of matte paper, flat and evenly lit with no highlights, no glare, and no dramatic lighting. Only the faintest fine grain and subtle crease texture visible across a uniform deep charcoal-black frame, edge to edge, no subject.

content.overlay_text: Let me take you back a few years.

content.text_html: I've been automating businesses for years. I've watched AI move through <accent>four eras.</accent>

content.text: The rule era. When this happens in one app, do that in another.
It worked. But it was rigid. It could only follow rules you wired by hand.

content.label: The catch
content.belief: The moment something changed, the automation just broke.

content.text: Now the automation could think a little. Write. Summarize. Decide.
But ChatGPT didn't know your business. And every step still had to be wired by hand.

content.label: The catch
content.belief: Smarter than before. But still generic, and still brittle.

content.name_html: Era Three: <accent>n8n and the first agents</accent>

content.text: AI you could hand a goal. And it would figure out the steps itself.
Real power. But fragile, hard to control, and it took an engineer to run.

content.label: The catch
content.belief: Closer. Still not something a business owner could actually use.

visual.prompt: A very dark, near-black surface covered edge to edge with a faint fine grid of thin dark-grey lines, like blueprint or graph paper, flat and perfectly evenly lit with no highlights and no glow, uniform minimal and technical across the entire frame, no subject.

content.overlay_text: This is the era that changes everything.

content.text: An AI that uses real tools, runs real tasks, and works inside your actual business.

content.claim_html: Not a chatbot you ask. <accent>A worker that does.</accent>

content.text: For the first time, AI can run the work, not just talk about it.

content.text_html: That was the moment it clicked: <accent>this isn't a better tool. It's a new operating system.</accent>

content.text: But I learned something else fast. Claude Code alone isn't enough. Three things have to be true.
The first thing everyone tries: one AI, doing all the jobs.
It writes your emails. Answers support. Looks at your numbers. All of it.

content.label: And it works, for about a week
content.belief: Then it gets confused. It mixes up its jobs. It forgets what you told it.

content.text: Here's why.

content.text_html: Every AI has a <accent>limited working memory.</accent> Ask one AI to do everything, and it drowns.

content.callout_html: An AI doing six jobs does all six <accent>badly.</accent> An AI doing one job does it like a specialist.

content.text: The fix is the same one every growing company discovers.

content.claim_html: You don't hire one person to do everything. <accent>You build a team of specialists.</accent>

content.step_description: Each agent owns a single function, and only thinks about that.
A specialist agent keeps its full attention on its own job. Nothing leaks or blurs.
Marketing passes to sales. Sales passes to support. Exactly like a real team.

content.wrong_text: A more powerful AI would fix the confusion.
content.correct_text: Even the smartest AI needs a defined role. Specialism beats raw horsepower.

content.text: We watched this play out across a hundred businesses.

content.headline: Split one overloaded AI into role-based agents. Quality jumped overnight.

content.text: Each agent stays sharp because it's never asked to be everything.
And because each one is focused, you can actually trust what it produces.

content.text_html: One AI is an assistant. <accent>A team of agents is an operating system.</accent>

content.text: So that's Lesson 1: you don't need a smarter AI. You need a team of focused ones.

content.label: But a team raises a new question
content.belief: Okay, but how does each agent actually know my business?

content.text: Good question.
Because a focused agent that knows nothing about you is still useless.
That's Lesson 2.

content.title: An Agent Is Only As Good As What It Knows

content.text: A specialist agent is powerful. But out of the box, it knows nothing about you.
Not your voice. Not your offers. Not your customers. Not your process.

content.label: So it does what untrained AI always does
content.belief: It guesses. And it sounds like the generic internet.

content.text: Here's the fix.
A brain is a knowledge base: your real information, written down where the agent can read it.

visual.prompt: A heavily darkened, low-key photograph of neatly stacked papers and printed documents on a dark surface, cinematic and muted. The stack and a soft pool of light are concentrated in the upper-right of the frame; the lower-left falls into deep shadow. The image fills the entire frame edge to edge with visible detail throughout and no large empty black areas.

content.overlay_text: Your winning ads. Your best emails. Your processes. Your numbers.

content.step_description: Your winners and your standards, collected into clean, structured files.
Each agent reads the brains relevant to its role. The marketer reads the brand brain.
Agents read from the same brains, so the whole team stays consistent.

content.wrong_text: You have to retrain the AI constantly.
content.correct_text: You update the brain. Every agent that reads it is instantly current.

content.callout_html: Generic AI writes the average of the internet. An agent with a brain writes <accent>like you.</accent>

content.text: This is what makes the output sound like your business, not a robot.

content.headline: We fed one client's brain 40 of their best emails. The next launch was AI-drafted, and it won.

content.text: And because brains are shared, sales knows what marketing promised. Support knows both.

content.text_html: Focused agents <accent>plus shared brains.</accent> Now you have a team that truly knows your business.

content.label: But there's still one problem
content.belief: If all of this lives on my laptop, only I can use it.

content.text: That's Lesson 3. And it's the one almost everyone misses.

content.title: If Only You Can Reach It, It's Not a System

content.text: Here's where almost everyone gets stuck.
You set up agents and brains on your computer. It works. It's incredible.

content.label: Then a teammate asks to use it
content.belief: And they can't. It only exists on your machine.

content.claim_html: A system only one person can reach <accent>isn't a system. It's a personal tool.</accent>

content.text: The fix is the last piece.

content.text_html: You host the whole thing <accent>in the cloud.</accent>

content.step_description: The agents and brains run on a server, not on anyone's laptop.
Marketing, sales, ops: everyone reaches the same agents and the same brains.
Routines run on schedule overnight. The system works while you sleep.

content.wrong_text: Cloud hosting is just a technical detail.
content.correct_text: It's the difference between a gadget you own and a company that runs on AI.

content.text: This is the step that turns it from your tool into your company's operating system.

content.text_html: Focused agents. Shared brains. Cloud-hosted for the whole team. <accent>That's the system.</accent>

visual.prompt: A very dark, near-black sheet of matte crinkled paper, flat even lighting with no glare and no bright spots, only subtle fine fold texture barely visible across a uniform deep charcoal-black frame, edge to edge, no subject.

content.overlay_text: So let me show you what it looks like when all three come together.

content.text: What we just covered was the WHAT.
The four eras. The three lessons. Why AI finally works inside a business.

Let me introduce you to the Friday Labs AIOS.
An AI Operating System, built on everything you just learned.

content.text: Every agent with its own brain, trained on your winners, reading shared knowledge.
All of it cloud-hosted, so your whole team works inside it from day one.

content.claim_html: Not software you bought. <accent>An operating system, built for you.</accent>
